newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt maintains poll lead over Oppn.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt maintains poll lead over Oppn.

text.p: Australia's Liberal-National government maintained its opinion poll lead over the Labor opposition in the latest poll published in Tuesday's edition of The Australian newspaper.
Support for the government and Labor opposition remained unchanged from the last poll two weeks ago at 51 percent and 34 percent respectively, The Australian's Newspoll found.
As preferred prime minister, John Howard's lead over opposition leader Kim Beazley fell to 32 points from 34 points in the last poll.
Howard's rating as preferred prime minister fell one point to 54 percent, while Beazley's rating rose one point to 22 percent.
The Newspoll surveyed 1,142 voters around the country by telephone over the last weekend.

The latest Morgan poll, conducted on the weekends of October 30 and November 6, said primary support for the government had fallen 0.5 percent to 49 percent from late October, while Labor's support rose one percent to 34 percent.
The government's two-party-preferred support fell 1.5 percent to 56.5 percent and Labor's support rose 1.5 percent to 43.5 percent, the Morgan poll found.
Under Australia's complicated preferential voting system, votes for minor candidates are redistributed to candidates with large numbers of votes according to preferences marked by voters.
The latest result compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 2 national election that ended 13 years of Labor rule.
